enonce_intro_markdown:
Two particles of mass $6\ \mathrm{kg}$ and $M\ \mathrm{kg}$ are connected by a light inelastic string passing over a fixed smooth pulley and then released from rest. The acceleration of the system is $5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

(Take $g$ as $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.)

Find,
incertitudes: Question 2 : le sujet ne dit pas laquelle des deux particules est la plus lourde. Les deux cas vérifient les données (M = 18 kg si M descend, M = 2 kg si M est la plus légère) ; le corrigé traite les deux et donne M = 18 kg comme lecture habituelle. Les réponses (d) et (e) sont les mêmes dans les deux cas ; (b) et (c) diffèrent (T = 90 N ou 30 N ; 180 N ou 60 N). Le sujet imprime « Take g as 10 m s^-2 » : valeur retenue g = 10.

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** Picture the pulley fixed to the ceiling with the string hanging vertically on each side; the string is light and inelastic and the pulley is smooth, so the tension $T$ is the same on both sides and the two particles have accelerations of equal magnitude $a = 5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ (one moves up, the other down). For each particle take the direction of its own motion as positive. $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

**Case 1: $M$ is the heavier particle** ($M$ descends, the $6\ \mathrm{kg}$ particle rises).

$$M\text{ (down):}\quad Mg - T = Ma$$

$$6\ \mathrm{kg}\text{ (up):}\quad T - 6g = 6a$$

Adding the two equations eliminates $T$:

$$(M - 6)g = (M + 6)a \;\Rightarrow\; 10(M - 6) = 5(M + 6) \;\Rightarrow\; 10M - 60 = 5M + 30 \;\Rightarrow\; M = 18$$

**Case 2: $M$ is the lighter particle** ($6\ \mathrm{kg}$ descends, $M$ rises).

$$6g - T = 6a,\qquad T - Mg = Ma \;\Rightarrow\; (6 - M)g = (6 + M)a \;\Rightarrow\; 60 - 10M = 5M + 30 \;\Rightarrow\; M = 2$$

The question does not say which particle is heavier, so both values satisfy the data. The usual reading, with $M$ the heavier particle, gives

**$M = 18\ \mathrm{kg}$** (the other possibility is $M = 2\ \mathrm{kg}$).

Using the equation for the $6\ \mathrm{kg}$ particle in Case 1 (it rises with acceleration $5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, positive upwards):

$$T - 6g = 6a \;\Rightarrow\; T = 6(10 + 5) = 90\ \mathrm{N}$$

Check with the $18\ \mathrm{kg}$ particle: $18\times 10 - T = 18\times 5 \Rightarrow T = 180 - 90 = 90\ \mathrm{N}$. Consistent.

**$T = 90\ \mathrm{N}$** (in Case 2, $M = 2$: $6g - T = 6a$ gives $T = 60 - 30 = 30\ \mathrm{N}$).

questions.enonce_markdown: the force exerted by the string on the pulley,
questions.corrige_markdown:
The string passes over the pulley and pulls on it along both of its vertical parts, each with tension $T$, both pulling downwards. The pulley is light and smooth, so these two pulls add:

$$F = 2T = 2\times 90 = 180\ \mathrm{N}\ \text{vertically downwards}$$

**Force on the pulley $= 180\ \mathrm{N}$ downwards** (in Case 2: $2\times 30 = 60\ \mathrm{N}$).

The system starts from rest ($u = 0$) with constant acceleration $a = 5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Using $v = u + at$:

$$v = 0 + 5\times 2 = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$

**$v = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$** (the heavier particle moves downwards, the lighter one upwards, both with this speed).

questions.enonce_markdown: the distance each mass travels in $2$ seconds.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The string is inelastic, so both masses move the same distance. Using $s = ut + \tfrac12 a t^2$ with $u = 0$:

$$s = \tfrac12\times 5\times 2^2 = 10\ \mathrm{m}$$

(Check: average speed $\tfrac{0 + 10}{2} = 5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, over $2\ \mathrm{s}$ gives $10\ \mathrm{m}$.)

**Each mass travels $10\ \mathrm{m}$** (one downwards, the other upwards).
